identity.title: Discovering Opinion Intervals from Conflicts in Signed Graphs

problem.claim: Infer a small, interpretable set of opinion intervals in signed graphs whose relationships are consistent with positive and negative interactions.

contributions.claim: Introduces an optimization formulation for opinion-interval inference, with hardness results and a polynomial-time approximation scheme linked to interval graphs and Correlation Clustering.
Provides scalable heuristics for computing opinion-interval solutions.
Applies the algorithms to German parliamentary co-voting data to recover parties’ political leaning.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper’s stated distinction is to formulate opinion-interval discovery from signed-graph conflicts and combine its analysis with interval-graph and Correlation Clustering connections.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their heuristics produce more expressive solutions than Correlation Clustering baselines in experiments.
In a German parliament case study, the authors report recovering political leaning from parties’ co-voting behavior using their algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Social-network conflicts are framed as potentially reflecting differing views and opinions.
The paper asks whether conflicts reveal a small, interpretable set of opinion ranges and formalizes this through signed graphs and sign-consistent intervals.
It presents an optimization problem with hardness results, a PTAS, scalable heuristics, comparative experiments, and a German parliament case study.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns the inferred object, the graph-sign consistency requirement, the optimization formulation, and the empirical comparison around one precise question.

lessons.interpretation: A tightly matched chain from interpretable target to formal constraint to evaluation criterion can make a methodological contribution easy to assess.
lessons.application: Define the desired latent structure and its observable consistency constraint before introducing the optimization objective, then evaluate with a baseline that represents the nearest competing formulation.
lessons.exception: This pattern is unsuitable when the target cannot be operationalized by a defensible observable constraint or when no meaningful baseline exists.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the hardness assumptions, approximation guarantee, heuristic details, or computational scales.
The experiments’ datasets, metrics, statistical results, and definition of “more expressive” are unspecified.
The German dataset’s size, construction, and validation of recovered political leaning are not reported.
